German Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul: 

"It must become clear over the next few days whether Russia is genuinely prepared to negotiate.

At this point in time, we do not see that. We only see murderous attacks against the completely innocent civilian population, who are suffering the most terrible things as a result.

We see absolutely no substantial contribution toward getting serious negotiations underway.

If that changes, everyone is prepared to engage very constructively. But Russia has not demonstrated that so far."

Ukraine will be represented at tomorrow's talks with Russia in Abu Dhabi by Foreign Intelligence Service chief Umerov, head of the Presidential Office Budanov, his first deputy Kyslytsya, Deputy chief of Ukraine's Defense Intelligence Skibitskyi, leader of the Servant of the People parliamentary faction Arakhamia, and an analyst from the Foreign Intelligence Service.

Russia will be represented by Medinsky, Ushakov, Deputy Foreign Ministers Ryabkov and Galuzin, head of the Main Directorate of Russia's General Staff Kostyukov, and deputy head of the General Staff's Main Operational Directorate Zhigarlovsky.

Before the two-day trilateral talks between Ukraine, Russia and the US in Abu Dhabi, Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff will meet with representatives of Ukraine, the EU, NATO, Germany, France, the UK and Italy. The discussions will focus on European security and Ukraine's postwar future.

Earlier, President Trump said peace in Ukraine was drawing closer and that he was working on a major agreement on Europe related to talks on a new European security architecture, which Trump's son-in-law Kushner already started on Wednesday during a meeting in Brussels with representatives of Europe and NATO. The discussion will continue on November 10-11 in Abu Dhabi between representatives of Ukraine, Russia, and the US.

According to the US, the Abu Dhabi negotiations will address post-war security guarantees for both Ukraine and Russia, as well as broader issues of creating a new European security architecture. The specific terms of the agreements under discussion remain unknown.

🇺🇸 The Nvidia scandal sent S&P 500 futures down $300 billion at market open. 6 minutes later, traders bought the dip and added back $350 billion.

But Jaspreet Singh, host of The Minority Mindset, says the real story isn’t the salacious affair, it's the bigger picture.

A handful of AI companies are carrying the entire market. And those companies are financing each other. 

Nvidia invests in OpenAI. OpenAI buys chips from Nvidia. The same money recycling between 15 companies, inflating valuations with every lap.

83% of S&P 500 companies are in correction territory. The index is hitting record highs anyway.

The parallels to 2008 and dot-com are eerie. Banks loosened lending to pile into the hot sector. Jamie Dimon says JPMorgan is already tightening. 

Cracks haven’t appeared yet, but they could soon.

Nvidia is the most valuable company in the world, so intertwined with every other AI company that one bad event ripples through all of them.

Too big to fail, on steroids...
